subject: Re: Order Form + Private Deployment Exhibit — license boundaries & audit routing
thread_summary: Customer sent redlines to Private Deployment exhibit requesting clarity on license scope and operator access. Internal team discussed compromise (snapshot + limited access window) and produced proposed contract language. Customer provisionally accepted with minor timing tweaks; asked for updated order form and on-site SOW.

To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: priya.suresh@canyonclinical.com, legal@canyonclinical.com
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment exhibit — redlines and auditor/escrow asks

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are our redlines (Canyon_CF_Redlines_v3.docx) to the Order Form + Private Deployment exhibit. A few high-level asks from our legal & infra teams:

- License scope: we need explicit language that the license covers our on-prem instance and any disaster-recovery snapshots for the duration of the Order Form.
- Operator access: we want a clear boundary for Redwood operator activity (read-only ops vs. ability to perform upgrades).
- Audit evidence: we may require periodic snapshots and a one-time remote witness during onboarding; can Redwood provide a binding playbook or evidence binder?
- Escrow-like alternative: we prefer an operational snapshot and attestation in lieu of full source code escrow; is that something Redwood will accept?

We're trying to keep this moving — target signature next week if we can close these items. Can you confirm which options Redwood supports and send suggested contract language?

Andrew
VP IT, Canyon Clinical

Andrew —

Thanks for the clear redlines. Short answer: yes, we can support a snapshot-based evidence path and a constrained operator boundary that meets most enterprise requirements. I'd like to propose a brief internal review to capture the exact wording and provide two options:

Option A (preferred): snapshot + attestation + limited remote witness window.
Option B (more conservative): dedicated operator access but only with mutually agreed SOPs (scoped upgrade/maintenance windows).

I'll pull together proposed language and loop in engineering and legal. If either option works for you in principle, tell me which you prefer and we'll draft language today.

I'll attach a draft annotated exhibit and the current Order Form for your review.

Best,
Lauren Bishop

Team —

Canyon Clinical (CN-4832) pushed redlines to the Private Deployment exhibit. Highlights below; need quick feedback so I can send firm language to the customer this afternoon.

Customer asks:
- License covers on-prem instance + DR snapshots for Order Form term.
- Prefer snapshot + attestation instead of source-code escrow.
- Wants clarity on operator access (no standing remote shell access; limited maintenance windows).

Questions for you:

- Aditya (Infra): operationally, can we produce a signed snapshot and provide a read-only verification session remotely? What does the witness session look like?
- Tessa (Compliance): what logs/evidence fields would satisfy a healthcare customer (audit trail, retention window, chain-of-custody)?
- Chloe (Product): do we need any feature gating or special runbook to support a customer witness?

Please reply in-line. Target: draft a compromise proposal by EOD today so we can keep the signature timeline.

Lauren

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Canyon Clinical redlines — suggested contract language

Lauren —

I've reviewed the redlines and propose a middle path we use frequently for regulated customers: a "Snapshot & Attestation" clause plus a tightly-scoped access SOP. High-level suggested language (draft):

"Snapshot & Attestation. In lieu of source code escrow, Redwood shall provide: (i) a read-only encrypted snapshot of the deployed image and supporting configuration artifacts; (ii) a certified attestation signed by Redwood's CTO attesting to the completeness of the snapshot; and (iii) a one-time remote witness session during initial onboarding to validate the snapshot contents. Redwood will retain chain-of-custody logs for each snapshot and make such logs available to the Customer upon reasonable request during the Term.

Operator Access. Redwood personnel shall have no standing remote shell or admin access to the Customer's on-prem environment. Maintenance activities requiring elevated privileges shall be performed only during mutually agreed maintenance windows and upon advance written notice. Emergency access may be permitted under a pre-approved emergency playbook with post-event notification and audit logs.

Audit Rights. The Customer may request up to two remote audit witness sessions per 12-month period. Additional sessions require a reasonable fee and 30 days' notice.

"

Operational notes for Aditya & Tessa:
- We should have a template attestation for signature (I'll draft).
- Aditya: are incremental snapshots feasible or do we provide full image snapshots at onboarding + quarterly?
- Tessa: recommend we include scope of logs (access, key management ops, KMS rotation records) and retention timeframe (12 months by default).

I'll attach an annotated exhibit with the redline language; suggest we offer Option A (snapshot + attestation + two witness sessions) as default. If the customer insists on operator access, we can escalate.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Private-Deploy-Exhibit-annotated.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Fwd: Proposed compromise language — Snapshot & Attestation (Order Form CN-4832)

Andrew / Priya —

Per our internal review, attached is a proposed compromise that should meet Canyon Clinical's needs while keeping the footprint of any operator access small. Key points:

- We propose "Snapshot & Attestation" in lieu of source-code escrow (see attached annotated exhibit).
- Redwood will provide a one-time remote witness during onboarding and up to two remote witness sessions per year.
- No standing operator shell access; maintenance performed during agreed windows; emergency playbook with post-event audit.
- We will produce chain-of-custody logs and a signed attestation of snapshot completeness.

If this aligns with what you need, please confirm and we will produce a final redline to the Order Form and Exhibit (OrderForm_CN-4832.pdf). If you prefer the Operator Access option, let us know and we'll escalate for a legal addendum.

Next steps we propose:
1) Customer confirms preference (Snapshot path vs Operator Access) by EOD Monday.
2) Redwood issues a clean redline within 48 hours.
3) Final review & signature.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Attachments: Private-Deploy-Exhibit-annotated.pdf (pdf), OrderForm_CN-4832.pdf (pdf)
